newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - Nov 6.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - Nov 6.

text.p: THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Federal Treasurer Peter Costello has denied Opposition suggestions the economy is flat. His comments came as speculation mounted that the Reserve Bank of Australia will cut official interest rates following its regular monthly board meeting. Speaking in question Time, the Treasurer hinted the current climate of wage restraint and low inflation provided a strong case for a Reserve Bank cut in rates. Page 3.

In a move which is expected to outrage countries such as Russia and India, the APEC forum is set to extend the controversial moratorium on new members by two to three years when members meet in the Philippines later this month. The summit is also expected to make reforms to the trade facilitation agenda, such as customs harmonisation and visa procedures for business people. Page 3.

In the fallout from the Federal Government's controversial decision to scrap research and development syndication tax concessions from July 23 this year, Orbital Engine Corporation yesterday initiated legal action against the Commonwealth to pursue its entitlement to tax concessions for its November 1995 application, worth A$14.5 million. Page 5.

Queensland Premier Rob Borbidge yesterday hit out at the State's independent watchdog, the Criminal Justice Commission, following CJC chairman Frank Clair's suggestions that the Borbidge Government was trying to "subvert" the role of the commission. The move has deepened Queensland's political crisis over allegations of corruption. Page 5.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Following the suicide of New South Wales Supreme Court judge David Yeldham QC, five days after he was named in State Parliament in connection with the Wood Royal Commission investigation into paedophilia, Australia's leading lawyers called last night for review of parliamentary privilege. Page 1.

The chairman of the Federal Government's defence review team, Malcolm McIntosh, unveiled plans yesterday to examine a series of radical options that could fundamentally change the command structure of the Australian Defence Force and the relationship between military and civilian bureaucrats. Page 3.

Amid concerns that Australian schools may be teaching too many mathematics and science concepts, the Federation of Australian Scientific and Technological Societies and the Australian Mathematical Sciences Council are to hold a top level forum later this month, which will bring together Government, industry and education groups, to outline the need for a restructuring of the school curriculum. Page 3.

The Federal Government's Australian Research Council has appointed 10 outstanding researchers as special investigators and awarded them a total of A$4.9 million to research their areas of speciality, such as a virtual geological time machine and a practical listing of ecological attributes of plant species. Page 3.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Following the suicide of former Supreme Court judge David Yeldham QC, who took his own life on Monday after discovering he had to be subpoenaed to appear before the Police Royal Commission's paedophile hearings, Commissioner Justice Wood appealed to the public to wait for his final report before passing judgement on the Commission's integrity. Page 1.

Bart Cummings' tremendous tenth Melbourne Cup win with Saintly, the horse he bred and trained to win the race, will only go a little way in helping Cummings dig himself out of A$29 million in debt, which he incurred in 1989 when a grand scheme to buy racecourses in bulk fell apart. Page 1.

Condemning New South Wales disability services as "light years behind the policies and programs in most other States", Council for Intellectual Disability director Phillip French has revealed a 14-year-old boy with intellectual disabilities has been living in "temporary" care facilities since 1989 due to policies which "border on the immoral". Page 3.

Local councils have had a partial win in their battle to control installation of pay-TV cables and mobile phone towers in their areas, with Communications Minister Richard Alston taking a submission to Cabinet this week arguing that the immunity currently enjoyed by Telstra and Optus concerning State and local planning laws should end in 1997. Page 3.
THE AGE

The race that stopped the nation was indeed Bart Cummings' race, as Australia's greatest horse trainer secured victory when the 8-1 chance Saintly streaked away from an international field to give Cummings his 10th Melbourne Cup. On a day which remained dry for the first time in a number of years and in front of a crowd of more than 90,000, Saintly won the prestigious race by two-and-a-quarter lengths from Count Chivas (33-1) and Skybeau (50-1), a head away for third. Page A1.

Former New South Wales Supreme Court Judge David Yeldham QC committed suicide hours after hearing he was to be subpoenaed to appear before the Wood Royal Commission's paedophile hearings. Police have revealed that in a suicide note left for his family, Yeldham, 67, referred to the Wood Royal Commission subpoena. Page A1.

Australian racing's biggest betting day was thrown into chaos yesterday when the Victorian TAB's central computer crashed for about three hours, resulting in the State's 288 betting agencies not being able to accept bets on the first five
races at Flemingon. Total betting on the Melbourne Cup in Victoria fell 10 per cent from last year with a total of A$18.6 million being spent. Page A2.

The former head of the Victorian Premier's Department, Ken Baxter, says he had special permission to receive more than A$70,500 in directors fees in addition to his A$270,000-a-year salary. Under Commonwealth laws he is required to pay earnings from his Australian Dairy Corporation position to the State. Page A3.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
